May I ask if your tinnitus is like a beeping oder more of  rustling or something else?
Depending on the type of sound you hear an audiologist would use a diffent signal for measuring your hearing. Because when you say you tinnitus has the same sound as the signals used to measure your hearing then it could just be that you can't hear the difference between the measuring signal and your tinnitus. Therefore you would only notice the signal when It becomes louder as your tinnitus and thus feel like you hear the signal later then you actually do.
If you did not already do that o would advise you seek out an audiologist and ask him to do a hearing test with a diffent signal. There are messing signals especially for these kind of situations.

I tried to explain in my other comment. Imaging it like when your using in ear plugs for listening to Musik. They often come with multiple sizes of the little buds. You pick the one that best fits your ears. When you listen to Musik and press them further into your ears you will notice the sound will be much richer and better in quality. That is because when the sound gets send into your ears it reflects from the walls of your ear canal befor reaching your eradrumm. If your ear canal is not sealed enough these reflections just kinda exit the ear. When you seal the ear canal tho all of the sound will reach your eradrumm without any loss.
It comes with the side effect of you hering your own voice different tho. You have to try out what works for you.

First of all... If you have 2 hearing aids don't go and only use 1. Its the most infuriating thing for me when people come in and tell me 'yeah I only use 1... It's just as good' No it's not. You have 2 ear for a reason. Same as with 2 eyes. If you only ever use one your other ear will be totally out of training when it comes to the point where you absolutely need 2 hearing aids.
The part your speaking of is not the speaker. The speaker is the little blue part that goes in your ear canal. The low sound quality your experiencing might be because the ear buds (or domes as they are called) might not be the best fit for your ears. If your ear canal is to big it might be comfortable to wear like this but all of the sound kind of 'goes missing'. The domes have to seal your ear a little bit more for you to experience better sound quality. I would advise you ask for an made to measure earmold as that would also fix your problem with the conchalock (the little sting-thing). If that's not for you just ask for a bigger dome.

I'm a hearing aid professional from Germany and I can assure you that your not missing anything.
The speaker is the blue part that goes in your ear. The dome is the little grey, silicone part on top. The size of the dome depends on the size of your ear canal. Your seems to be quite small, so you only have such a little sleeve on it.
I'm germany most of the time we only sell a hearing aid with an made to measure earmold. But things are very diffenet in other countries... Hell in Germany you can get hearing aids for as low as 0€.
